audit.whatIsWrong: EVEN 5.5/10 is right, but the level chart disagreed with itself across the two layers.
audit.why: 54.18% over 4557 games. Naafiri owns levels 2-5 (packmates plus Eviscerate at 11/10/9/8/7s beat Fizz's pre-6 string), Fizz owns 6 onward. The packet levelChart is [Fizz, Naafiri, Naafiri, Naafiri, Fizz, Fizz, Fizz] and the content win[] row matches it exactly — the full-layer phases[].side read [Naafiri, Skill, Skill, Skill, Fizz, Skill, Skill], so six of seven rows contradicted the content layer.
audit.corrected: All six full-layer sides moved onto the packet/content verdict, with phases[1..3].why rewritten to describe Naafiri winning those stages.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text was directionally right and already named her pattern.
audit.why: Fizz: level 3 pole, level 6 Chum the Waters, first item. Naafiri: level 2 extra packmate, Hounds' Pursuit at 110/95/80s with a shielded recast. The flip at 6 is real because Playful/Trickster's untargetability answers a lock-on dash.
audit.corrected: Left the spikes[] array alone; breakdown.spikes kept.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three real interactions were absent: Fizz's passive vs packmates, Playful/Trickster's grounding vs her dashes, and what Eviscerate actually heals.
audit.why: Fizz's passive moves through units, so packmates cannot body-block him — the old advice to 'stand near minions to body-block the hounds' is advice for the wrong champion. Fizz E carries the grounding flag and Naafiri's Q leap, E and R all carry dash; the slam denies her exit. Riot's Eviscerate text reads that it recalls her packmates 'and fully healing them' — the heal is on the pack, not on Naafiri, so chip damage into hounds is wasted and Naafiri herself is the target.
audit.corrected: Written into tradeGood, breakdown.mid, breakdown.carry and dosFull[1].d.

audit.why: Hounds' Pursuit 110/95/80s, Eviscerate 11/10/9/8/7s, Fizz E 16/14/12/10/8s all come from the kits.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the real numbers and her punishable window named.
